symptoms.symptom: Freezer door pops open when refrigerator door is closed

causes.label: This is normal if, after popping open, the freezer door closed on its own.
remedies: This indicates that there is a good seal on the freezer door.
If the freezer door does not automatically close after popping open, the rollers need adjusting.
See Rollers and Leveling Legs.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 19: "This is normal if, after popping open, the freezer door closed on its own."

symptoms.symptom: Door does not close by itself

causes.label: Leveling legs need adjusting.
remedies: See Rollers and Leveling Legs.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 19: "Leveling legs need adjusting."

symptoms.symptom: Refrigerator does not operate

causes.label: Refrigerator in defrost cycle.
remedies: Wait about 40 minutes for defrost cycle to end.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 19: "Refrigerator in defrost cycle."

causes.label: Refrigerator control in 0 (off) position.
remedies: Move the refrigerator and freezer control to a temperature setting.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 19: "Refrigerator control in 0 (off) position."

causes.label: Refrigerator is unplugged.
remedies: Push the plug completely into the outlet.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 19: "Refrigerator is unplugged."

causes.label: The fuse is blown/circuit breaker is tripped.
remedies: Replace fuse or reset the breaker.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 19: "The fuse is blown/circuit breaker is tripped."

symptoms.symptom: Vibration or rattling (slight vibration is normal)

causes.label: Refrigerator is not resting on all four rollers.
remedies: Adjust leveling legs (See Rollers and Leveling Legs).
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 19: "Refrigerator is not resting on all four rollers."

symptoms.symptom: Motor operates for long periods or cycles on and off frequently (Modern refrigerators with more storage space and a larger freezer require more operating time. They start and stop often to maintain even temperatures.)

causes.label: Normal when refrigerator is first plugged in.
remedies: Wait 24 hours for the refrigerator to completely cool down.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 20: "Normal when refrigerator is first plugged in."

causes.label: Often occurs when large amounts of food are placed in refrigerator.
remedies: This is normal.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 20: "Often occurs when large amounts of food are placed in refrigerator."

causes.label: Door left open.
remedies: Check to see if package is holding door open.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 20: "Door left open."

causes.label: Hot weather or frequent door openings.
remedies: This is normal.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 20: "Hot weather or frequent door openings."

causes.label: Temperature controls set at the coldest setting.
remedies: See About the controls.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 20: "Temperature controls set at the coldest setting."

symptoms.symptom: Refrigerator or freezer compartment too warm

causes.label: Temperature control not set cold enough.
remedies: See About the controls .
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 20: "Temperature control not set cold enough."

causes.label: Warm weather or frequent door openings.
remedies: Set the temperature control one step colder.
See About the controls.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 20: "Warm weather or frequent door openings."

causes.label: Door left open.
remedies: Check to see if package is holding door open.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 20: "Door left open."

causes.label: Freezer door popped open.
remedies: See the problem Freezer door pops open when refrigerator door is closed.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 20: "Freezer door popped open."

symptoms.symptom: Frost or ice crystals on frozen food (frost within package is normal)

causes.label: Door left open.
remedies: Check to see if package is holding door open.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 20: "Door left open."

causes.label: Too frequent or too long door openings.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 20: "Too frequent or too long door openings."

causes.label: Food blocking freezer air vents.
remedies: Move items away from the back wall of the freezer.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 20: "Food blocking freezer air vents."

symptoms.symptom: Frequent “buzzing” sound

causes.label: Icemaker power switch is in the I (on) position, but the water supply to the refrigerator has not been connected.
remedies: On power switch models, set the power switch to the O (off) position.
On feeler arm models, move the feeler arm to the STOP (up) position.
Keeping the power switch in the I (on) position or the feeler arm in the ON (down) position will damage the water valve.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 20: "Icemaker power switch is in the I (on) position, but the water supply to the refrigerator has not been connected."

symptoms.symptom: Small or hollow cubes

causes.label: Water filter clogged.
remedies: Replace filter cartridge with new cartridge or with plug.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 20: "Water filter clogged."

symptoms.symptom: Automatic icemaker does not work (on some models)

causes.label: Icemaker power switch is not on.
remedies: On power switch models, set the power switch to the I (on) position.
On feeler arm models, move the feeler arm to the ON (down) position.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 20: "Icemaker power switch is not on."

causes.label: Water supply turned off or not connected.
remedies: See Installing the water line.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 20: "Water supply turned off or not connected."

causes.label: Freezer compartment too warm.
remedies: Wait 24 hours for the refrigerator to completely cool down.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 20: "Freezer compartment too warm."

causes.label: Piled up cubes in the storage bin cause the icemaker to shut off.
remedies: Level cubes by hand.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 20: "Piled up cubes in the storage bin cause the icemaker to shut off."

causes.label: Ice cubes stuck in icemaker. (Green power light on icemaker blinking.)
remedies: Turn off the icemaker, remove cubes and turn the icemaker back on.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 20: "Ice cubes stuck in icemaker. (Green power light on icemaker blinking.)"

symptoms.symptom: Ice cubes have odor/taste

causes.label: Ice storage bin needs cleaning.
remedies: Empty and wash bin.
Discard old cubes.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 20: "Ice storage bin needs cleaning."

causes.label: Food transmitting odor/taste to ice cubes.
remedies: Wrap foods well.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 20: "Food transmitting odor/taste to ice cubes."

causes.label: Interior of refrigerator needs cleaning.
remedies: See Care and cleaning.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 20: "Interior of refrigerator needs cleaning."

symptoms.symptom: Slow ice cube freezing

causes.label: Door left open.
remedies: Check to see if package is holding door open.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 20: "Door left open."

causes.label: Temperature control not set cold enough.
remedies: See About the controls.
A newly installed refrigerator may take 12–24 hours to begin making ice cubes.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 20: "Temperature control not set cold enough."

symptoms.symptom: Moisture forms on cabinet surface between the doors

causes.label: Not unusual during periods of high humidity.
remedies: Wipe surface dry; then adjust the fresh food control setting one number higher and check again in 24 hours.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 20: "Not unusual during periods of high humidity."

symptoms.symptom: Refrigerator has odor

causes.label: Foods transmitting odor to refrigerator.
remedies: Foods with strong odors should be tightly wrapped.
Keep an open box of baking soda in the refrigerator; replace every three months.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 20: "Foods transmitting odor to refrigerator."

causes.label: Interior needs cleaning.
remedies: See Care and cleaning.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 20: "Interior needs cleaning."

symptoms.symptom: Refrigerator compartment light does not work

causes.label: No power at outlet.
remedies: Replace fuse or reset the breaker.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 20: "No power at outlet."

causes.label: Light bulb burned out or loose.
remedies: See Replacing the light bulbs.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 20: "Light bulb burned out or loose."

symptoms.symptom: Moisture collects inside (in humid weather, air carries moisture into refrigerator when doors are opened)

causes.label: Too frequent or too long door openings.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "Too frequent or too long door openings."

causes.label: Open containers of water or warm food in the refrigerator.
remedies: Cover or seal open containers.
During a defrost cycle, moisture will be removed from the refrigerator, but may return with long or frequent door openings.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "Open containers of water or warm food in the refrigerator."

symptoms.symptom: Food freezing in the refrigerator

causes.label: Food too close to the air vent at the back of the refrigerator.
remedies: Move the food away from the air vent (near the controls).
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "Food too close to the air vent at the back of the refrigerator."

causes.label: Refrigerator control is set too cold.
remedies: Move the refrigerator control to a warmer temperature setting one increment at a time.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "Refrigerator control is set too cold."

symptoms.symptom: Orange glow in the freezer

causes.label: Defrost heater is on.
remedies: This is normal.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "Defrost heater is on."

symptoms.symptom: Door bins do not fit in the door

causes.label: The freezer door bins are a different size than the refrigerator door bins.
remedies: Try to install the bins in both doors.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "The freezer door bins are a different size than the refrigerator door bins."

symptoms.symptom: Freezer light does not work

causes.label: Some models do not have a freezer light.
remedies: Check for a semi-clear dome light shield in the freezer ceiling.
If the dome is opaque white, the model does not have a freezer light.
Check for a door activated light switch on the right side of the freezer.
If there is only a cap in place of a switch, the model does not have a freezer light.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "Some models do not have a freezer light."

causes.label: Light bulb burned out or loose.
remedies: See Replacing the light bulbs.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "Light bulb burned out or loose."

symptoms.symptom: Controls do not light up

causes.label: Some models do not have lighted controls.
remedies: If you can read white numbers on the control setting, the model does not have lighted controls.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "Some models do not have lighted controls."

causes.label: Refrigerator light bulb burned out or loose.
remedies: See Replacing the light bulbs.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "Refrigerator light bulb burned out or loose."

symptoms.symptom: Ice bucket does not fit under the icemaker

causes.label: The freezer shelf is in the top position.
remedies: Place the shelf in the lower position.
See Rearranging the shelves.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "The freezer shelf is in the top position."

symptoms.symptom: Water has poor taste/odor

causes.label: Water dispenser has not been used for a long time.
remedies: Dispense water until all water in system is replenished.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "Water dispenser has not been used for a long time."

symptoms.symptom: Water in first glass is warm

causes.label: Normal when refrigerator is first installed.
remedies: Wait 24 hours for the refrigerator to completely cool down.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "Normal when refrigerator is first installed."

causes.label: Water dispenser has not been used for a long time.
remedies: Dispense water until all water is system is replenished.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "Water dispenser has not been used for a long time."

causes.label: Water system has been drained.
remedies: Allow several hours for replenished supply to chill.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "Water system has been drained."

symptoms.symptom: Water dispenser does not work

causes.label: Water supply line turned off or not connected.
remedies: See Installing the water line.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "Water supply line turned off or not connected."

causes.label: Water filter clogged.
remedies: Replace filter cartridge or remove filter and install plug.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "Water filter clogged."

causes.label: Air may be trapped in the water system.
remedies: Run 11/2 gallons from the dispenser to clear the system
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "Air may be trapped in the water system."

symptoms.symptom: Water spurting from dispenser

causes.label: Newly-installed filter cartridge.
remedies: Run 11/2 gallons from the dispenser to prevent spurting
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "Newly-installed filter cartridge."

symptoms.symptom: Water is not dispensed but icemaker is working

causes.label: Water in reservoir is frozen because the controls are set too cold.
remedies: Set the refrigerator control to a warmer setting and wait 24 hours.
If water does not dispense after 24 hours, call for service.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "Water in reservoir is frozen because the controls are set too cold."

symptoms.symptom: No water or ice cube production

causes.label: Supply line or shutoff valve is clogged.
remedies: Call a plumber.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "Supply line or shutoff valve is clogged."

causes.label: Water filter clogged.
remedies: Replace filter cartridge or remove filter and install plug.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "Water filter clogged."

causes.label: Filter cartridge not properly installed.
remedies: Remove and reinstall filter cartridge, being certain that it locks into place.
The blade on the end of the cartridge should be positioned vertically.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "Filter cartridge not properly installed."

symptoms.symptom: Water is leaking from dispenser

causes.label: Glass not being held under the dispenser long enough after button is released.
remedies: Hold the glass underneath the dispenser for 2–3 seconds after releasing the dispenser button.
Water may continue to dispense after the button is released.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "Glass not being held under the dispenser long enough after button is released."

causes.label: Air may be present in the water line system, causing water to drip after being dispensed.
remedies: Run 11/2 gallons from the dispenser to remove air from from the system.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "Air may be present in the water line system, causing water to drip after being dispensed."
